description: Remote-mode line-break flattening. Every real line or paragraph break (LF U+000A, CR U+000D, LINE SEPARATOR U+2028, PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR U+2029) is replaced by a single space, and a run of consecutive breaks (CRLF, blank lines, mixed) collapses to one space. Nothing else changes: existing spaces are not collapsed, nothing is trimmed, and the two-character text backslash-n is not a break. A literal newline delivered into a terminal surface is Enter, so any break that survived would submit a dictated prompt half-typed; only the separate, explicit Enter may submit.
function: RemoteControlService.flattenLineBreaks(in:) — input string in, flattened string out
verifiedBy: Characterization of the Swift implementation (spec #93, ticket #120); Tests/PowerUpTests/TextSafetyFixtureTests.swift. Pure function, independent of any cmux or terminal version.

cases.name: empty input
cases.reason: Empty dictation must stay empty, not turn into a stray space typed into the session.

cases.name: no breaks is untouched
cases.reason: Ordinary text must arrive byte-for-byte unchanged.

cases.name: LF becomes a space
cases.reason: A dictated LF would act as Enter and submit 'run the tests' alone before the rest arrives.

cases.name: CR alone becomes a space
cases.reason: CR is what a terminal's Enter key actually sends; a bare CR inside the text submits early.

cases.name: CRLF becomes one space, not two
cases.reason: Windows-style pasted text must not submit early nor leave a double space where one break was.

cases.name: U+2028 line separator becomes a space
cases.reason: Rich-text sources and some recognisers emit LINE SEPARATOR; terminals may treat it as a line break.

cases.name: U+2029 paragraph separator becomes a space
cases.reason: PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR from rich-text paste must not split the prompt.

cases.name: blank line between paragraphs collapses
cases.reason: A blank line (two LFs) is still one break; it must become one space, not two Enters.

cases.name: mixed run of every break kind collapses to one space
cases.reason: Mixed-source paste can stack different break kinds; the whole run is one gap in the prompt.

cases.name: separate breaks each become their own space
cases.reason: Breaks separated by text are flattened independently; no word is glued to the next.

cases.name: trailing LF becomes a trailing space
cases.reason: A trailing newline from dictation or paste would submit on its own; it is flattened (not trimmed), and submission is left to the explicit Enter.

cases.name: trailing CRLF becomes a trailing space
cases.reason: Copied lines usually end in CRLF; the pair must not survive as a premature submit.

cases.name: trailing U+2029 becomes a trailing space
cases.reason: A rich-text paragraph end at the end of the prompt must not submit early.

cases.name: leading LF becomes a leading space
cases.reason: A leading newline would submit an empty prompt before the real text arrives.

cases.name: only breaks become a single space
cases.reason: Input made of nothing but breaks must not press Enter several times in the target session.

cases.name: existing spaces around a break are kept
cases.reason: Flattening only replaces breaks; it does not collapse or trim the user's own spacing.

cases.name: tab is not a line break
cases.reason: Tab is outside the flattened set; only line and paragraph breaks are rewritten.

cases.name: vertical tab, form feed and NEL are not flattened
cases.reason: The flattened set is exactly LF, CR, U+2028 and U+2029; widening it silently would change what other characters are typed.

cases.name: literal backslash-n text is not a break
cases.reason: The two characters backslash and n are text, not a break; defusing them for cmux is segmentation's job, not flattening's.

cases.name: CJK text with a line break
cases.input:
运行测试
然后提交
cases.expected: 运行测试 然后提交
cases.reason: Chinese dictation broken across lines must arrive as one prompt with its characters intact.

cases.name: emoji surrogate pairs either side of a break
cases.reason: Astral-plane characters (UTF-16 surrogate pairs) next to a break must not be split or mangled.

cases.name: ZWJ emoji sequence with CRLF
cases.reason: A multi-scalar emoji sequence must stay whole when the break after it is flattened.

cases.name: a break a combining mark follows is still flattened
cases.reason: Flattening works on scalars, not characters: a combining mark after a newline must not shield it from becoming a space (condense, a display rule, keeps such a break; injection never may).
